title: Service: FastAPI job API, moto-tested S3 store, Pareto frontier endpoint

questions.heading: Snapshots and Results Live in S3, Job States in a Local SQLite File
questions.stem: A client posts the same validated portfolio twice to the snapshot endpoint. What is in the bucket's snapshots afterwards?

options.text: One object, since the second post finds its key and writes nothing
options.says: Right: the `exists` check finds `snapshots/<digest>.json`, and the demo counted one object.

options.text: Two objects, since each post is a new version of the snapshot
options.says: The key is the content's digest, and the demo printed "objects in S3: 1".

options.text: No object, since a snapshot is stored only when a job first solves it
options.says: The snapshot endpoint stores it and answers 201 with its digest, before any job.

options.text: One object, since S3 refuses a second write to a key that already exists
options.says: S3 would accept the write and replace the object; the `exists` check is what skips it.

questions.heading: A Job Is Accepted at Once, Polled, Then Fetched
questions.stem: A client submits a medium job and asks for its result in the very next request, while the job is still running. What does the service answer?

options.text: 202 again, since the job was accepted and is still being worked on
options.says: 202 is the submit's answer; the fetch of an unfinished job answered 409 in the demo.

options.text: 404, since no result object exists in S3 for the job yet
options.says: 404 means no such job; the job exists, so the fetch answers 409.

options.text: 409, since the result does not exist yet, with the job's current state
options.says: Right: the demo's "fetch at once -> 409", and the reply says the job's state.

options.text: 200 with status queued, since every fetch returns the job's latest record
options.says: The fetch returns the result only once the job has finished; before that it answers 409.

questions.heading: The Frontier Endpoint Returns Only Non-Dominated Plans
questions.stem: Three floors give three plans: NPV $100k with risk removed $50k, NPV $98k with risk $60k, and NPV $97k with risk $55k. Which does the frontier endpoint return?

options.text: All three, since each is the best plan for its own floor
options.says: The endpoint drops any point another point dominates.

options.text: The first two, since the second has more of both than the third
options.says: Right: $98k and $60k beat $97k and $55k on both objectives, so the third is dominated.

options.text: Only the first, since it has the most NPV of the three
options.says: The second has more risk removed than the first, so neither dominates the other.

options.text: Only the second, since it has the most risk removed of the three
options.says: The first has more NPV than the second, so it is not dominated either.
